name.text: WAT 11.1: HashMap Goes on a Diet!

questiontext.text:
Goal

A canteen calorie board stores one number for each dish. Staff add, correct, and remove dishes during the week. Water remains a valid entry with a calorie count of zero.

Read
  • Go maps in action. Under "Declaration and initialization", what value does an uninitialised map variable have? What happens if you write to it? Which two forms create a writable map?
  • In the same section, find what kind of type a map is. If a caller passes a map to post, what can the function change?
  • Under "Working with maps", how do you read a value? What do you get for a missing key? Which built-in removes an entry? What happens if that key is absent?
Coming from Java

Java uses new HashMap<>(), followed by methods such as put, getOrDefault, and remove. The separate get method returns null for a missing key.

Map<String, Integer> board = new HashMap<>();
board.put("soup", 120);
int kcal = board.getOrDefault("cake", 0);
board.remove("water");
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If newBoard panics, check the value of m under "Declaration and initialization".
  • Find delete on the page and read the sentence after its example.

testcode.text: b := newBoard() post(b, "roll", 210) post(b, "roll", 190) strike(b, "water") fmt.Println(b, len(b))
b := newBoard() strike(b, "cake") fmt.Println(lookup(b, "cake"), lookup(b, "water"), len(b))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A cattle brand is a registered mark that identifies a herd. The district brand book stores the number of cattle for each brand. A sold-out herd has a count of zero, while an unregistered brand has no entry. Registering a brand that is already in the book leaves its count alone. A new brand starts at zero head.

Read
  • Index expressions. Find "For a of map type M". What is a[x] when the map has no entry for x? What is a[x] when the map is nil?
  • Below the type parameter rules, find the special assignment form for a map index. What extra value does it produce? When is that value true?
Coming from Java

Java code might use book.get(brand) == null or containsKey. The get method distinguishes a missing key from a stored zero by returning null. Go has neither method.

Integer head = book.get(brand);
if (head == null) return "unregistered";
Banned: len, range
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • The special assignment form fits in the short statement of an if, as in WAT 05.2.
  • Find the sentence beginning "The value of ok is". Which returned value distinguishes each case in status?

testcode.text: book := map[string]int{"lazy-k": 12, "bar-x": 0} register(book, "lazy-k") register(book, "bar-x") fmt.Println(status(book, "bar-x")) fmt.Println(status(book, "lazy-k"), book)

expected.text: registered, no stock registered, 12 head map[bar-x:0 lazy-k:12]

questiontext.text:
Goal

A raffle gives each buyer one or more numbered tickets. The village records each buyer's name and ticket count. On Friday, the notice board must list them in the same order on every run.

Read
  • slices.Sort. Read the signature and first sentence. What does the call return? In which order does it leave x?
  • Go maps in action, section "Iteration order". In what order does a range loop visit map keys? Can the next loop use a different order?
  • Comparison operators. Find how Go compares two strings. Based on that rule, does capital B come before or after lowercase a?
Coming from Java

Java offers new TreeMap<>(tickets) for a sorted view. Another option is keySet().stream().sorted() when the map must remain a HashMap. Go's standard library has no sorted map type.

for (String name : new TreeMap<>(tickets).keySet())
    System.out.println(name + " x" + tickets.get(name));
Required: slices.Sort
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Check the "Iteration order" example. Replace its sorting call with the one named on the red line.
  • holders already sorts the names. Let notice loop over the result from holders instead of the map.

expected.text: [ana cole hemi maia rangi tui] ana x1 cole x3 hemi x2 maia x1 rangi x2 tui x5
[Bob Zoe adam] [] 0 Bob x1 Zoe x1 adam x2
